title: Double Buffering
body:
Two frame buffers instead of one. The display hardware scans out the **front** buffer
while your code draws the next frame into the **back** buffer; when the frame is finished
you swap which one is which.

The problem it solves is **tearing**. The screen is scanned out progressively, so drawing
into the buffer currently being displayed means the top of the visible frame is old and
the bottom is new, with a visible seam where the scan line caught up with you. Worse if
you clear the buffer first: the viewer sees the image being built.

The swap has to happen when nothing is being scanned, which is the vertical blanking
interval between the last line of one frame and the first line of the next. That is why
the swap lives in the [[VBL ISR]] rather than in the drawing loop, and why frame rate ends
up locked to the refresh rate.

Same idea as the [[Buffering]] on an [[I-O Interface]], one buffer filling while the other
drains, applied to pixels.
